primary.title: Ordinary Portland Cement - Specification (Sixth Revision)
primary.summary: IS 269 : 2015 merged the earlier 33, 43 and 53 grade OPC standards into one. It covers ordinary Portland cement in grades OPC 33, OPC 43, OPC 53 and the sulphate-resisting-blend grades OPC 43S and OPC 53S. It specifies chemical requirements (lime saturation factor, alumina-iron ratio, insoluble residue, magnesia, sulphuric anhydride, loss on ignition, chloride), physical requirements (fineness, soundness by Le Chatelier and autoclave, setting time, compressive strength at 3, 7 and 28 days) and packing and marking.

certification.summary: All cement manufactured or sold in India is under compulsory BIS certification through the Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003. An OPC 43 grade plant must hold a BIS Scheme I licence for IS 269 and mark every bag / consignment with the ISI mark and the CM/L number.

applicable.name: Scheme I (ISI Mark Scheme)
applicable.covers: Licence to use the ISI mark on OPC to IS 269 after assessment of the cement plant and testing of samples for the full chemical and physical requirements, including 28-day compressive strength.
applicable.why: Cement under the Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003 requires full ISI-mark certification with a plant Scheme of Inspection and Testing and continuous quality control.
applicable.you_receive: A BIS licence with a CM/L number and the right to mark bags and bulk consignments with the ISI mark and grade (e.g. OPC 43); normally valid for 2 years and renewable.

not_applicable.name: Scheme II (CRS)
not_applicable.why: CRS is only for MeitY-notified electronics and IT goods. Cement is a construction material under Scheme I.

not_applicable.name: Scheme X
not_applicable.why: Scheme X is for machinery/equipment to a purchaser's specification, not for a bulk building material.

testing.summary: Samples are drawn from the plant and tested at a BIS / BIS-recognised laboratory against IS 269 using the IS 4031 and IS 4032 methods. Because 28-day strength takes 28 days, the licence timeline is dominated by the strength test. The plant runs daily routine tests under its SIT.

tests.name: Setting time (initial and final by Vicat)
Compressive strength at 3, 7 and 28 days
tests.condition: Type test + routine test (28-day is the governing test)

tests.name: Chemical requirements: LSF, alumina-iron ratio, insoluble residue, MgO, SO3, loss on ignition, chloride
Heat of hydration / air content (where specified)

sources.doc: BIS Product Manual PM/IS 269 - tests and SIT
BIS Compendium of Cement Standards (IS 4031, IS 4032 methods)

labs.note: Cement testing needs a laboratory with IS 269 / IS 4031 / IS 4032 in its recognised scope and a cement testing setup (compression machine, Blaine apparatus, Le Chatelier, chemical lab). Confirm scope in the BIS LIMS directory. Many large plants have their own BIS-recognised in-house labs.

licensing.summary: Scheme I (ISI mark) licence for OPC to IS 269 is applied for online on Manak Online: apply and pay -> scrutiny -> plant inspection and sample drawal -> independent testing (including 28-day strength) -> grant of licence with the CM/L number.

steps.title: Apply online on Manak Online
steps.detail: Register the firm, file the Scheme I application for IS 269 with the grade(s) applied for (e.g. OPC 43), upload documents, declare the SIT and in-house laboratory, and pay the fee.

steps.title: Scrutiny of application
steps.detail: BIS verifies the plant process (raw mill, kiln, cement mill, packing), quality control set-up and in-house lab, and raises queries.
steps.timeline: About 15-30 days after a complete application

steps.title: Plant inspection and sample drawal
steps.detail: A BIS officer inspects the plant and laboratory, witnesses routine tests and seals samples for independent testing.

steps.title: Independent testing against IS 269
steps.detail: Full chemical and physical testing at a BIS / recognised lab; the 28-day compressive strength test sets the minimum duration.
steps.timeline: About 5-6 weeks (dominated by the 28-day strength test)

steps.title: Grant of licence
steps.detail: On a satisfactory inspection and test report, BIS grants the licence and CM/L number for the grade; bags/consignments may then be ISI-marked. Licence normally valid 2 years, renewable.
steps.timeline: Commonly around 4 to 5 months from a clean application

documents.summary: Documents for the Scheme I application for OPC 43 to IS 269. Conditional items depend on the firm's constitution and grades applied for.

items.name: Firm / plant establishment proof
items.explanation: Company registration, GST, factory licence, industrial licence / consent to operate, and plant address proof.

items.name: Manufacturing process flow chart and machinery list
items.explanation: Quarry, raw mill, kiln, clinker storage, cement mill, packing plant, with capacity.

items.name: In-house laboratory equipment list with calibration certificates
items.explanation: Compression testing machine, Blaine apparatus, Vicat, Le Chatelier, autoclave, XRF / wet chemistry for the SIT.

items.name: Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT)
items.explanation: Daily routine test plan for clinker and cement, lot definition, retained-sample policy and records.

items.name: Recent internal test data / trend charts for the grade
items.explanation: 3, 7 and 28-day strength and chemistry trends demonstrating consistent conformance to IS 269 for OPC 43.

items.name: Bag / marking artwork
items.explanation: Proposed bag printing showing the ISI mark, grade (OPC 43), CM/L number, week and year of packing and net mass.

items.name: Authorised signatory authorisation and ID
items.explanation: Board resolution and ID of the person signing the application.

items.name: Importer: Authorised Indian Representative (AIR) papers
items.explanation: Foreign cement manufacturers apply through an AIR with appointment letter and undertakings.
